approach: 1) Find files with identical basenames across folders. 2) Diff suspect pairs. 3) Check for v1/v2/legacy/old/_bak prefixes. 4) Compare obvious structural parallels (Requests/ vs PaymentRequests/).

explicit_intentional_dual_files_per_owne.description: Per audit prompt — POS Vanilla pos-wizard.js + Kiosk Vue Kiosk*.vue compose the same business logic via two UI surfaces by DESIGN. Not flagged.

candidates.title: PaymentGateways/Requests/<Name>.php vs PaymentGateways/PaymentRequests/<Name>.php — twin folders, 22 paired class files
paths_left: app/Http/PaymentGateways/Requests/Bkash.php (and 21 others: Cashfree, Easypaisa, Flutterwave, Iyzico, Mercadopago, Midtrans, Mollie, Myfatoorah, Payfast, Paypal, Paystack, Paytm, Pesapal, Phonepe, Razorpay, Senangpay, Skrill, Sslcommerz, Stripe, Telr, TwoCheckout)
candidates.diff_stat: Same class names, DIFFERENT bodies. Requests/* contains real validation rules ($request->bkash_status check, app_key/secret rules etc). PaymentRequests/* are STUBS: spot-checked Cashfree/Razorpay/Senangpay all return rules() => [] (empty array). The only PaymentRequests/* with any rule is Stripe.php which validates 'stripeToken' => required|string|max:190.

actual_runtime_usage.Requests/<Name>.php: Loaded dynamically by Admin/PaymentGatewayController.php:37 for admin gateway-settings update (validates admin form input with real rules)
actual_runtime_usage.PaymentRequests/<Name>.php: Loaded dynamically by Frontend/PaymentController.php:75 which calls $request->validate($gateway->rules()). For all gateways EXCEPT Stripe, rules() returns an empty array, so the customer's payment-form payload is effectively unvalidated at this layer (server-side validation may exist downstream in the gateway service classes themselves — not verified by this audit).

candidates.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS but FLAG-FOR-OWNER-CONFIRMATION — both folders are wired to different controllers, so deleting either would break runtime. HOWEVER the PaymentRequests/* stubs suggest an architectural intent that may have been left incomplete: either the stubs are intentional (downstream gateway services handle validation) or there is a latent validation gap on the customer payment payload. Owner should confirm whether the empty rules() bodies are intentional design or unfinished work.
candidates.user_friendly: Two folders with the same class names. The admin-side folder (`Requests/`) has full validation. The customer-side folder (`PaymentRequests/`) is mostly empty stubs that return no rules — only the Stripe stub has one rule (the Stripe token format). This may be intentional (the actual gateway code may validate further downstream) but it is worth a quick owner glance: 'is this empty-stub pattern on purpose, or did somebody forget to fill in the rules?'. Either way, do NOT delete the files — Frontend/PaymentController.php loads them by name at runtime, so removing breaks payment immediately.

examples: MenuComponent: admin/settings/MenuComponent.vue (admin CRUD) vs frontend/menu/MenuComponent.vue (customer-facing menu display)
ItemComponent: admin/items/ (admin CRUD), admin/pos/ (POS picker), frontend/components/ (customer card), table/components/ (dine-in card) — 4 distinct variants
OfferComponent, CouponComponent — admin manage vs frontend display
AddressComponent: frontend/checkout/ (one-shot pick) vs frontend/account/address/ (account-level CRUD)
candidates.diff_stat: All radically different files — they share a name token but no body overlap. This is naming convention not duplication.
candidates.verdict: KEEP-AS-IS — these are separate components with different responsibilities. NOT duplicates. Naming convention is internally consistent (Admin/* = manager UI, Frontend/* = customer UI, table/* = dine-in UI, kiosk/* = self-service UI).
candidates.user_friendly: Lots of Vue components share names like 'MenuComponent' or 'ItemComponent' but they are different files for different surfaces (admin CRUD vs customer view vs POS picker vs dine-in card). All are legitimate. Renaming for clarity is a nice-to-have, not a duplication problem.
